references.text: The nations heard about Israel's exodus from Egypt and trembled with fear, showing how God placed dread among the nations before His people.
God promises to send His terror ahead of Israel and confuse all the peoples they encounter, paralleling the promise in Deuteronomy.
Moses repeats the promise that fear and dread for Israel will come upon every land they set foot on.
Rahab confirms that the people of Canaan were filled with fear and trembling because of what they had heard about Israel's God.
The kings of the Amorites and Canaanites lost heart when they heard how the Lord had dried up the Jordan for Israel.
God's terror fell upon the cities around Jacob, so that they did not pursue his sons—an early example of this principle.
Egypt rejoiced when Israel left, because fear of them had fallen upon the Egyptians.
